scope.chart_change: nil-safe migrationSecret compatibility fix in this evidence commit
scope.topology: single-node K3s with host-local external data services

operator_role.name: atp
operator_role.note: The bootstrap operator remains superuser because PostgreSQL will not allow it to demote itself.

redis.keys_and_channels: limited to ATP, Celery queues, replies, pidbox and celeryev patterns
redis.worker_ping: passed for default and performance workers

minio.policy: bucket-scoped application object read/write/delete and multipart operations

issues_found_and_fixed.issue: Helm --reuse-values omitted the newly introduced migrationSecret map and caused template evaluation to fail before an upgrade.
issues_found_and_fixed.fix: Guard migrationSecret and existingName with nested with blocks; add a regression contract and null-value render check.
issues_found_and_fixed.result: Revision 42 compatibility upgrade and revision 43 least-privilege upgrade succeeded.

issues_found_and_fixed.issue: The initial Redis ACL omitted Celery priority-suffixed queue keys, reply/pidbox keys and celeryev channels.
issues_found_and_fixed.fix: Add only the observed queue, reply, pidbox and event patterns, persist users.acl and restart the real Redis service.
issues_found_and_fixed.result: Both worker pools respond, the backup task completes and the final ACL denial count is zero.

rollback.note: Rollback must restore the matching runtime Secret and Helm revision together; credentials are intentionally not recorded in this evidence.

remaining_release_boundaries: Redis is RDB-only and AOF remains disabled.
MinIO is on the same host and has no independent backup endpoint.
MinIO versioning and lifecycle policy remain release decisions.
Release-level Prometheus, long-term SLO and alert evidence are still missing.
C3 empty-database migration, upgrade and rollback drill remains open.
